name: blackswan-events
description: The MACRO-EVENT probe — event-CONDITIONED trading (the B2 line, exogenous triggers). The intraday probe measured UNCONDITIONAL short-horizon direction as null; this asks a narrower, genuinely exogenous question: in the window right after a SCHEDULED macro release (CPI, jobs, retail, PCE, GDP), does the crypto reaction PERSIST (event_drift) or REVERSE (event_fade) far enough to clear the ~0.2% round trip? A scheduled release is external information the price could not have fully priced a bar earlier, so if any short-horizon drift is real anywhere, the minutes after a release are where it should live. The probe trades ONLY in event windows (few trades/day), the 'recognise the condition, trade only then' discipline — so unlike the continuous probes its cost is low. It reuses the shared point-in-time release timing (pit_fusion: release date + the series' publish wall-clock, DST-aware) and the intraday backtest mechanics, so every existing gate/lens/scorecard reads an event cell unchanged. Guards pinned before any number is emitted: (a) an event fires at the series' real RELEASE datetime, NEVER the reference period it describes (refPeriod-stamping is the classic macro look-ahead); only GENUINE discrete releases are events — the daily rate series (DFEDTARU/DFF/DGS10/...) are excluded since a value every calendar day is not a market event; coincident releases across series collapse to one event; (b) the reaction bar is the FIRST decision bar at/after the release, its return is known at that bar's close and the position is applied to the NEXT bars, never the reaction bar's own return; event times are fixed by the macro calendar and never depend on price. NOTE: because the strategy is in-market only briefly, return_vs_hold_pct is structurally biased against it in a trending year; the EXPOSURE-NEUTRAL decider is signal_expectancy (per-trade edge net of cost) alongside oos_sharpe. Deterministic and model-free (the seed is contract-only).

asset.description: Which crypto instrument's 1m price is resampled, traded and benchmarked. return_vs_hold_pct and beta/up/down capture are measured against THIS asset over the same span. The macro events themselves are asset-independent (US macro releases).

bar.description: Decision-bar width in minutes: the 1m series is resampled up to this cadence and the post-release reaction is measured on these bars. A smaller bar catches the immediate reaction (and a tighter hold); a larger bar a slower one.

signal.description: The reading of the post-release reaction. event_drift RIDES the first post-release bar's move (information persists); event_fade FADES it (overreaction correction). The reaction bar is the first decision bar at/after the release; its move is ridden/faded and the position applied to the NEXT bars. An unknown value is refused, so a typo can never file one arm's result under the other's label.

event_group.description: Which scheduled releases are events. cpi = CPI NSA+SA (~12 unique/yr); jobs = payrolls + jobless claims + unemployment (~60/yr); macro_all = those plus retail sales, core PCE, GDP (~90/yr). Only GENUINE discrete releases — the daily rate series are excluded. Coincident releases across series collapse to one event. FOMC is deferred (needs a real meeting calendar, not a daily rate print).

hold_bars.description: How many decision bars a position is held after the reaction bar, then flat. The position earns bars b+1..b+hold_bars (never the reaction bar's own return), and a new event inside the hold window is ignored. Sweeps the horizon over which any post-release drift would have to persist to clear cost.

transaction_fee.description: Per-side fee, charged on turnover at entry and again at exit, so a round trip costs ~(1-fee)^2 ≈ 0.2% at the default. Because the probe trades only a few times per WEEK, realized_cost_bps is low — the cost floor is not the enemy here, the per-trade edge is.

walk_forward_window.description: Which out-of-sample span is ACCOUNTED. Only events (and bars) inside the test window enter the metrics; the month before it is a formation lookback for an event opening just before the span. alt-2024 and alt-2025 are the two fully-mined crypto windows shared by all three assets, both fully covered by the macro release history.

seed.description: Present for contract conformance only — the backtest is fully deterministic, so seeds are not swept (identical cells would fake replication).
